chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: Declining work, British tour and refusing travel to stay with her daughter
summary: The tour was an exception to fewer bookings; after stopping in '57 she didn't accept offers.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Okay, and you cut two sides? with Vic Ash
Okay, and then when you got back to the States - did you find, you just said this was coming towards the end of a period where you were finding fewer satisfactory work situations.
Was that tour an exception to this pattern?

Well, the opportunity to travel, you know, to Europe, to tour the British Isles was quite an experience and how would I have gotten there any other way? I had a good time. And I worked on bills with ten or twelve acts you know. This is an experience too.

This is really variety, they call it over there. In the United States it was called vaudeville. There were all tumblers, kinds of acts, comedians, what have you.
Did you have alot of opportunities to travel which you turned down because, let's say, you have a young daughter?

Well not really. When I stopped in '57 I just didn't except, I mean, I just didn't answer the phone if you want to know the truth. I wasn't getting that many calls to begin with and I wasn't trying. I just cut it off because you got to make up your mind what you're going to do. If you're going to quit, quit. You're not being true to yourself. And as I said before, I figured I had had it. I was very satisfied with the fact that I had accomplished something in twenty years and it didn't bother me a bit. And I got really involved in the school situation. I was anxious to learn more, you know. I got in there and found a new interest and I enjoyed it.
